Troubleshooting · BEGINNER FRIENDLY · 5 MIN READ

Bluetooth won’t connect? Start here.

Tech Compass · Updated 2026-10-19

IN THIS GUIDE

The quick answer1. Check power and distance2. Check existing connections3. Pair againStill not connecting?Further reading
THE QUICK ANSWER

Charge the accessory, put it into pairing mode, and check whether it is already connected to another device. Bluetooth being switched on is not the same as being discoverable.

1. Check power and distance

Charge both devices and place them close together. Follow the accessory manual to enter pairing mode; the usual power button action may only turn it on.

2. Check existing connections

Headphones may reconnect automatically to a nearby phone. Disconnect them there, then try pairing with the intended device. Some accessories support multiple connections; others do not.

3. Pair again

In Bluetooth settings, remove the failed pairing only if you know how to pair the accessory again. Restart the accessory and add it as a new device. On Windows, use Settings → Bluetooth & devices; on a phone, open its Bluetooth settings.

Still not connecting?

Test with another compatible device. If the accessory works elsewhere, check the original device’s supported updates and Bluetooth troubleshooting. Use your manufacturer’s drivers rather than third-party driver-download tools.
